name: incident_dataset
description: GenAI Data Security Incident Database. Real-world data security incidents in GenAI systems, one per record, mapped to the DSGAI risk taxonomy. Each record is either 'public' (a publicly disclosed incident that names the affected organization and cites public sources) or 'anonymized' (a self-report with no organization names).
citeAs: OWASP GenAI Data Security Initiative. GenAI Data Security Incident Database (version 1.0.0). OWASP GenAI Security Project. https://github.com/GenAI-Security-Project/GenAI-Data-Security-Initiative/tree/main/datasets/incident_dataset
rai:dataBiases: Skews toward incidents that security researchers publicise, especially prompt injection against assistants and agents, and toward English-language sources.
Organizations that disclose openly appear more often than those that do not.
rai:dataCollection: Public entries are written by contributors from public sources: vendor advisories and post-mortems, CVE records, researchers' disclosures, regulator notices and reputable press. Summaries are in the contributors' own words and stay within what the cited sources state. Anonymized entries are contributor self-reports.
rai:dataLimitations: Small and not exhaustive: a curated sample of disclosed incidents, not a census.
Public entries are only as complete as their sources; vendor-internal details are usually unknown.
Research demonstrations and vulnerability disclosures are included alongside confirmed breaches; the summary says which.
DSGAI mappings are expert judgments reviewed by peers.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Maintained by the OWASP GenAI Data Security Initiative (Workstream 5). Contributions arrive as pull requests and must pass data_validation/run_all_checks.py in CI and peer review; weekly online checks re-verify cited CVEs, advisories and links. Versioned releases carry SHA-256 checksums.
rai:dataSocialImpact: All public incidents are already disclosed; the dataset aggregates them so defenders can learn from them. Naming organizations is limited to what public sources state.
rai:dataUseCases: Grounding GenAI data-security threat models and training in real incidents mapped to DSGAI.
Linking incidents to the crosswalk incident list and to the vulnerability and exploit datasets.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal data about individuals: people's names are not allowed. Public entries name organizations only as the affected or responsible party, as their cited sources do.
